questions.question_english:
Consider the following Assertion (A) and Reason (R).
Assertion (A): A linguistic minority institution can deny admission to students of the majority community entirely to preserve its linguistic character.
Reason (R): Article 30(1) grants minorities the absolute right to administer their institutions without any state interference in admission policies, provided they receive no state aid.
options_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation_english: A linguistic minority institution cannot completely deny admission to non-minority students; absolute exclusion violates Article 29(2) if state-aided, and judicial rulings prohibit total exclusion even in unaided settings. Statement R correctly notes that Article 30(1) protects administration, but that right is subject to overall non-discrimination principles, making A false.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर D है। अनुच्छेद 30(1) अल्पसंख्यक संस्थानों को अपनी पहचान बनाए रखने और प्रशासन करने का अधिकार देता है, लेकिन यह पूर्णतः निरंकुश अधिकार नहीं है। गैर-अल्पसंख्यक विद्यार्थियों को पूरी तरह बाहर करना हर स्थिति में संवैधानिक रूप से स्वीकार्य नहीं माना जा सकता; सहायता-प्राप्त संस्थानों पर अनुच्छेद 29(2) के गैर-भेदभाव नियम भी लागू होते हैं। इसलिए अभिकथन गलत है और कारण में पूर्ण स्वायत्तता का दावा भी सही नहीं है—स्रोत की कुंजी को final में अलग से verify करना आवश्यक है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) A is false but R is true

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: A linguistic minority institution cannot completely deny admission to non-minority students; absolute exclusion violates Article 29(2) if state-aided, and judicial rulings prohibit total exclusion even in unaided settings. Statement R correctly notes that Article 30(1) protects administration, but that right is subject to overall non-discrimination principles, making A false.

questions.question_english: Under the Right to Information Act (an implicit extension of Article 19(1)(a)), a Principal of a Government School functions as a:

Public Information Officer (PIO)

questions.explanation_english: Under the Right to Information Act, 2005 (which derives authority from Article 19(1)(a)), heads of public authorities like government school Principals are designated as Public Information Officers (PIOs). key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Public Information Officer (PIO)

Consider the following pairs of concepts and their constitutional basis:
I. Free and compulsory education up to age 14: Article 21A
II. Instruction in mother tongue at primary stage: Article 350A
III. Early childhood care and education for children below 6 years: Article 41 Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?

questions.explanation_english: Article 21A guarantees free elementary education up to age 14, and Article 350A encourages primary instruction in the mother tongue. Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Article 21A guarantees free elementary education up to age 14, and Article 350A encourages primary instruction in the mother tongue. Assertion (A): Article 350A makes it legally binding and enforceable through courts for every State to provide primary education strictly in the mother-tongue.

questions.question_english:
Examine the following statements about the role of the State in promoting education under the Directive Principles:
I. The State is directed to make effective provision for securing the right to education, within the limits of its economic capacity and development.
II. The State shall endeavor to promote international peace and security through education.
III. The State shall protect monuments of national importance. Which of the above are explicitly mentioned in Part IV of the Constitution?
options_english: I and II
I and III
II and III
I, II and III
questions.explanation_english: Part IV Directive Principles encompass securing the right to education (Article 41), promoting international peace and security through education (Article 51), and protecting monuments of national importance (Article 49). questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर है: I, II और III। भाग IV के नीति-निदेशक सिद्धांतों में अनुच्छेद 41 राज्य की आर्थिक क्षमता और विकास की सीमाओं के भीतर शिक्षा सहित कुछ अधिकारों को प्रभावी बनाने के प्रावधानों से संबंधित है। अनुच्छेद 51 अंतरराष्ट्रीय शांति और सुरक्षा को बढ़ावा देने का निर्देश देता है, जबकि अनुच्छेद 49 राष्ट्रीय महत्त्व के स्मारकों और स्थानों की रक्षा से संबंधित है। इसलिए तीनों कथन भाग IV के संवैधानिक विषयों से मेल खाते हैं।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) I, II and III

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Part IV Directive Principles encompass securing the right to education (Article 41), promoting international peace and security through education (Article 51), and protecting monuments of national importance (Article 49). key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Moved 'Education' to the Concurrent List.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976 transferred 'Education' from the State List (List II) to the Concurrent List (List III) under Entry 25. questions.question_english: Read the situation below and answer the question that follows: A private unaided school established by a linguistic minority denies admission to a student from a different linguistic community, stating they have zero seats for outsiders. Under the interpretation of Article 30(1) by the Supreme Court:
options_english: They possess an absolute, unrestrictable constitutional right to reserve 100% of seats exclusively for their own community.
Aided schools cannot deny entry under Article 29(2); unaided schools have autonomy but can admit non-minorities.
They are legally bound by constitutional mandate to reserve at least 50% of their total student capacity for non-minority candidates.
They are prohibited from giving any preference or priority to applicants from their own community during the admission process.
questions.explanation_english: State-aided minority schools are bound by Article 29(2) and cannot deny admission on grounds of religion or language. While unaided minority schools possess autonomy under Article 30(1), judicial rulings establish that they cannot operate as exclusive enclaves and may admit non-minority applicants up to reasonable proportions.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर है: सहायता-प्राप्त विद्यालय अनुच्छेद 29(2) से बँधे होते हैं; गैर-सहायता प्राप्त संस्थानों को स्वायत्तता होती है, लेकिन वे गैर-अल्पसंख्यक विद्यार्थियों को भी प्रवेश दे सकते हैं। अनुच्छेद 29(2) राज्य द्वारा संचालित या राज्य सहायता प्राप्त संस्थानों में केवल धर्म, नस्ल, जाति या भाषा के आधार पर प्रवेश से वंचित करने पर रोक लगाता है। गैर-सहायता प्राप्त अल्पसंख्यक संस्थानों को प्रवेश और प्रशासन में अधिक स्वायत्तता मिल सकती है, लेकिन अनुच्छेद 30(1) का अर्थ यह नहीं कि उनके पास हर परिस्थिति में 100 प्रतिशत सीटें अपने समुदाय के लिए आरक्षित करने का अप्रतिबंधनीय अधिकार है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Aided schools cannot deny entry under Article 29(2); unaided schools have autonomy but can admit non-minorities.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: State-aided minority schools are bound by Article 29(2) and cannot deny admission on grounds of religion or language. While unaided minority schools possess autonomy under Article 30(1), judicial rulings establish that they cannot operate as exclusive enclaves and may admit non-minority applicants up to reasonable proportions.

questions.explanation_english: Article 22 provides protection against arbitrary arrest and detention, mandating that arrested persons must be informed of grounds, allowed legal counsel, and produced before a magistrate within 24 hours.
